createdAt.description:
Shows results only from the selected range of days.
Multiple values allowed, separated by comma.
Values can be exact number of days or range of days.
Use the following pattern where n is an integer in a range of 0<=n<=MaxInt : 
'n': exact number of days.
'n-n': range of days.
'-n': from n days ago until now.
'n-': from n days ago and before.
Example: created-at=5,10-20,30-,-2.
Summary: results from exactly 5 days ago, results from 10 to 20 days ago, results from 30 days ago and above, results from 2 days ago until now.
createdAt.name: created-at

post.description:
Use this API to create an "asignment". An "assignment" specifies one or more "entities" (user, usergroup, or OAuth Client) and grants them permission to access specific "resources" (tenant, application or project). The request body is a JSON object that defines all of the relevant parameters for the assignment.
> To use this API, you must have permission `update-access` for all resources related to this assignment. > Currently, the set of actions that a user can take on each resource is determined by the permissions that they have accross the tenant account. In a later phase, it will be possible to assign granular permissions relative to specific resources.

get.description: Multi-action form of /get-resources. Returns, for each requested action, the resources of the given types that are assigned to the current user (as identified by JWT token). Actions granted by the same set of roles are resolved together, so asking for many actions in one request costs substantially less than issuing one request per action. Note the response is not deduplicated: two actions resolving to the same resources each carry their own copy of the list.

get.description:
Retrieves the AI triage result for a vulnerability group within a project. To retrieve a triage result, you must specify the project's identifier (`project_id`) and the identifier of the vulnerability group (`group_id`). If triage has completed, the endpoint returns the full analysis, including the triage verdict, summary, confidence score, and supporting details. If processing has not yet completed, the endpoint returns the current job status. If the triage operation failed, the endpoint returns a failed job status. > The recommended way to obtain the `group_id` is to call [**`GET /api/risks`**](RiskOrchestration.yaml/paths/~1/get) for the specified project and use the `groupId` field of the corresponding risk object. > > If necessary, you can construct the `group_id` manually: > > - **SCA:** Construct the value using the following format: >
> `#-##-#` >
> Where: > - `similarityId` is the vulnerability's `similarityId` returned by `GET /api/results`. > - `packageIdentifier` is the package identifier (`data.packageIdentifier`) returned by `GET /api/results`. > - `projectId` is the project identifier used in this request. > > - **SAST:** Use the `similarityId` returned by `GET /api/sast-results`. If your SAST scanner is configured to group similar results by **Attack Vector ID**, use the `attackVectorID` instead. > **Important:** If the `group_id` contains reserved URL characters (such as `#`), URL-encode the value before using it as a path parameter. For example, replace each `#` with `%23`.

**Important:** Each update will only affect the instances of the images in the specific Project you identify. If the same images exist in other Projects as well, they will remain unaffected.

post.description:
Use this API to retrieve logs of the different triaging actions performed on a particular image, package, or vulnerability.
### Audit Logs Hierarchy The Audit Logs are returned based on the following hierarchy: **Image → Package → Vulnerability (CVE)** The API accepts up to three identifiers: | field | meaning | |-------------|-------------------------------------| | `imageId` | the specific image | | `packageId` | a software package inside that image | | `cveId` | a vulnerability associated with that package | Only **one** is required to be provided to the API. ### Rules | inputs provided | result returned | |-------------------------------------|-----------------| | `imageId` only | only **image** audit logs | | `packageId` only | only **package** audit logs | | `cveId` only | **not allowed** — `packageId` is required together with `cveId` | | `packageId` + `cveId` | CVE events + parent package events | | `imageId` + `packageId` | package events + parent image events | | `imageId` + `packageId` + `cveId` | CVE events + parent package events + parent image events | All multi-layer results are sorted in **descending order** by event date. ### Example ```json { "imageId": "nginx:latest", "packageId": "Oval#-#libcrypto3#-#3.1.4-r5#-#alpine", "cveId": "CVE-2022-40993" } ``` This means: return audit logs for this CVE, plus the parent package, plus the parent image — all together — newest first.

parameters.name: projectId

parameters.description: Id of the scan for which this log is being retrieved

post.description:
Specify the KPI for which you would like to retrieve results (required) and specify the filter settings to apply to the request (optional). > Each request can return data for only a single KPI. To retrieve multiple KPIs, send a separate request for each one. The following KPIs are available via this API: - **vulnerabilitiesBySeverityTotal** - returns the number of vulnerabilities of each severity level (Critical, High, Medium, Low and Info). - **vulnerabilitiesByStateTotal** - returns the number of vulnerabilities in each state (To Verify, Not Exploitable, Proposed Not Exploitable, Confirmed and Urgent). - **vulnerabilitiesByStatusTotal** - returns the number of vulnerabilities in each status (New, Recurrent and Fixed). - **vulnerabilitiesBySeverityAndStateTotal** - returns counters for vulnerabilities broken down by the combination of severity and state. - **vulnerabilitiesBySeverityOvertime** - returns counters for vulnerabilities broken down by severity for each time included in your time range. - **meanTimeToResolution** - for each severity level and state, this returns the number of results and the mean time that it took to resolve them. - **fixedVulnerabilitiesBySeverityOvertime** - returns the number of `critical` and `high` vulnerabilities fixed at each time included in your time range. - **ideOvertime** - returns analytics on scan activity of IDE plugins over time, categorized by IDE. Data includes number of unique developers who executed scans in the specified time period and the total number of scans run per time unit. - **ideTotal** - similar to ideOvertime, but returns overall totals across the specified period, rather than values segmented by time unit. - **agingTotal** - returns vulnerability counts grouped by age category (e.g., 0–30 days, 31–60 days, etc.). For each age category, the response includes total count of vulnerabilities in that range and a breakdown by severity level. - **allVulnerabilities** - returns all vulnerability counts grouped by vulnerability names, broken down by severity.
*Note:* `limit` and `offset` are required fields for this KPI. The limit value must be between 1 and 1000. - **mostCommonVulnerabilities** - returns a list of the vulnerabilities most commonly found in your projects, with the total number of instances as well as a breakdown by severity.
*Note:* `limit` is a required field for this API. The limit value must be between 1 and 100. - **mostAgingVulnerabilities** - returns a list of the oldest unresolved vulnerabilities.
*Note:* `limit` is a required field for this API. The limit value must be between 1 and 100. > For KPIs that return results over time, datapoints are broken down into different units depending on the length of the time range, as follows:
range < 1 minute → 1 second
range < 1 hour → 1 minute
range < 1 day → 1 hour
range < 1 week → 1 day
range < 6 month → 1 day
range < 1 year → 1 month
## Limitations - Data is only available for the previous year. - Returns results for SAST, SCA, IaC Security, Container Security and DAST scanners. > The "Send API Request" feature is not currently supported in this platform.

post.description:
Use this API to create a new preset for a specific scanner.
### Defining a preset
To define a preset, you submit an array of objects, one per query family you want to include.
Each object declares:
- `queryFamily` — the family name (e.g. ASP, Apex, CSharp)
- `totalCount` — number of queries included
- `queryIds` — the list of query IDs from that same family that should be included in this preset

You may **only list IDs that actually belong to the declared family.**
If you do not include any queries from a given family, you **simply omit that family** from the array.
> To retrieve a complete list of Query Families and the details of the queries in each family, use [`GET /api/preset-manager/{scanner}/query-families`](reference/Preset-Manager.yaml/paths/~1{scanner}~1query-families/get) and [`GET /api/preset-manager/{scanner}/query-families/{query-family}/queries`](reference/Preset-Manager.yaml/paths/~1{scanner}~1query-families~1{query-family}~1queries/get).

This API supports different query and override request body types for the following scanners:
- **SAST**
- **KICS** (IaC Security)
- **Secret Detection**

Use this API to create a new query or override the query source of an existing query.
- To create a new query, submit the relevant **Create Query Request** body documented below. All queries are created on the tenant level of your Checkmarx account.
- To override a query source, submit the relevant **Override Query Request** body documented below. Use the `level` field to define whether this override applies to the tenant, project, or application level.
> All queries are created in the context of an active Audit Session. For a walkthrough of how to create an active session, see [here](https://checkmarx.stoplight.io/docs/checkmarx-one-api-reference-guide/xpannu2qcp7qx-query-editor-service-rest-api#workflow)

Run queries in your Audit Session, with or without a `source`.

The request body accepts an array of query objects, where each object must include a `queryId` and may optionally include a `source`.

**Run with original source.**
If a query object does not include the `source` field, the query runs using the **source** saved for that query.

**Override the source.**
If a query object includes the `source` field, the query will run using the specified source.

**Multiple queries.**
You may submit one or more query objects in the same request. Each query can independently run with its saved source or an overridden source.
> This API returns a request ID that you can use to see the results of the query execution. Use this ID with the [`Retrieve status of a specific request`](https://checkmarx.stoplight.io/docs/checkmarx-one-api-reference-guide/61ebupyxatxt3-retrieve-status-of-a-specific-request) API.

Handle POST /remediate requests.

This endpoint triggers remediation for one or more scan results (same scan).
The request is validated automatically by FastAPI/Pydantic.
Authentication is handled by the get_jwt_claims dependency.

Args:
    request: The validated remediation request body.
    response: FastAPI response object for setting headers.
    correlation_id: Correlation ID from header or generated.
    claims: JWT claims containing tenant_id and user_id.
    tenant_id: Same as ``claims.tenant_id``; provided separately so
        ``@feature_flag_enabled(..., tenant_id_param="tenant_id")`` can bind the
        route parameter by name.
    handler: The remediate handler injected via dependency.

Returns:
    AcceptedResponse: 202 Accepted response. ``published`` is ``true`` when a new
        remediation pipeline event was published and ``false`` on an idempotent
        duplicate; ``existingState`` then reports the duplicate's state
        (``"processing"`` or ``"completed"``) and is ``null`` when ``published`` is true.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 400 if the scan's source code is no longer available in RepoStore.
    HTTPException: 401 if authentication fails or required claims are missing.
    HTTPException: 403 if the feature flag, license, or role checks deny access.
    HTTPException: 503 if SecurityContext was not initialized (e.g. missing middleware).
    HTTPException: 402 if consumption enforcement is on and credits are insufficient.
    HTTPException: 503 if consumption enforcement is on and CGWS is unavailable.
    HTTPException: 500 if publishing to RabbitMQ fails.

post.description:
Convert a manual Checkmarx One project to a Code Repository project. The POST method must be submitted with a request body that specifies the Code Repository project configuration as well as info about each project that is being connected to a repo. You can convert multiple projects with a single API call. However, each conversion process can only connect to repos within a particular organization. Also, you can only run a single conversion process for each organization (specified by `scmType` and `orgIdentity`). > For integrations using our Self-Hosted flow, the initial step of creating a code repository instance (by submitting an Instance Name, URL, and authentication credentials) must be done via the UI before you can use this API to migrate projects. >
For integrations using the GitHub Apps Cloud Hosted flow, the organization must first be [imported via the UI](https://docs.checkmarx.com/en/34965-466709-code-repository-integration-using-github-app.html#UUID-0815e8fd-8adf-de68-eb42-5bf35405a6b6_UUID-8d2bc53d-d714-a301-9f7e-ba86e777dd2f) before you can use this API to migrate projects. > The success response includes a **ProcessId** which is used to check the status of the conversion using the [GET Retrieve conversion status](projectConversion.yaml/paths/~1project-conversion/get) API. > The "Send API Request" feature is not currently supported in this platform.

post.description:
This API is a monitoring endpoint that allows clients to check whether the update predicates process is currently running for a given set of **similarity ID**s or **attack vector ID**s within a specific scan.

Designed to support the **AI Triage** feature, it enables users to verify whether bulk triage operations are still in progress before attempting to update results, helping avoid conflicts or stale data during concurrent operations.

The endpoint accepts a **scanID** and an array of **similarResultsIDs**, and returns a boolean indicating whether any update is actively running, along with the grouping mode (Similarity ID or Attack Vector ID) currently configured for the tenant.

packageVulnerabilities.description: In JUnit4 from version 4.7 and before 4.13.1, the test rule TemporaryFolder contains a local information disclosure vulnerability. On Unix like systems, the system's temporary directory is shared between all users on that system. Because of this, when files and directories are written into this directory they are, by default, readable by other users on that same system. This vulnerability does not allow other users to overwrite the contents of these directories or files. This is purely an information disclosure vulnerability. This vulnerability impacts you if the JUnit tests write sensitive information, like API keys or passwords, into the temporary folder, and the JUnit tests execute in an environment where the OS has other untrusted users. Because certain JDK file system APIs were only added in JDK 1.7, this this fix is dependent upon the version of the JDK you are using. For Java 1.7 and higher users: this vulnerability is fixed in 4.13.1. For Java 1.6 and lower users: no patch is available, you must use the workaround below. If you are unable to patch, or are stuck running on Java 1.6, specifying the `java.io.tmpdir` system environment variable to a directory that is exclusively owned by the executing user will fix this vulnerability. For more information, including an example of vulnerable code, see the referenced GitHub Security Advisory.

post.description:
Use this API to create a configuration for accessing a private repo.
### Submitting Configuration Content
The request body must contain the configuration `content`. Use the relevant template below and replace the placeholder values with your real credentials.
> The `<MASK_NAME>` placeholder is simply the name you assign to your integration account during setup. See [Step 1 - Setting up an Integration](https://docs.checkmarx.com/en/34965-365191-jfrog-artifactory-integration-for-sca-scanner.html#id480095) for where this name is defined. 

#### Templates (per package manager)
<details>
<summary>Nuget</summary>

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<configuration>
  <packageSources>
    <add key="nuget.org" value="https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json" />
    <add key="Artifactory" value="${{cx.<MASK_NAME>.url}}/artifactory/api/nuget/v3/automatedtests-nuget/" />
  </packageSources>
  <packageSourceCredentials>
    <Artifactory>
      <add key="Username" value="${{cx.<MASK_NAME>.username}}" />
      <add key="ClearTextPassword" value="${{cx.<MASK_NAME>.password}}" />
    </Artifactory>
  </packageSourceCredentials>
</configuration>
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>Maven</summary>

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<settings xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/SETTINGS/1.2.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/settings-1.2.0.xsd" xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/SETTINGS/1.2.0"
    xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
  <servers>
    <server>
      <id>jfrog</id>
      <username>${{cx.<MASK_NAME>.username}}</username>
      <password>${{cx.<MASK_NAME>.password}}</password>
    </server>
  </servers>
  <profiles>
    <profile>
      <id>artifactory</id>
      <repositories>
        <repository>
          <id>central</id>
          <name>cx-virtual</name>
          <url>${{cx.<MASK_NAME>.url}}/artifactory/automatedtests-maven/</url>
          <snapshots>
            <enabled>true</enabled>
          </snapshots>
        </repository>
      </repositories>
    </profile>
  </profiles>
  <activeProfiles>
    <activeProfile>artifactory</activeProfile>
  </activeProfiles>
</settings>
```
</details>

<summary>NPM</summary>


```ini

email = ${{cx.<MASK_NAME>.username}}
always-auth = true
@checkmarx:registry=${{cx.<MASK_NAME>.url}}/artifactory/api/npm/automatedtests-npm/

post.description:
### Overview Run a scan on one of the following resources: **Zip archive**, **Git repo**, or **Confluence**. In each scan you can run one or more of the following Checkmarx scanners: - ZIP archive or Git Repo: **SCA, SAST, Containers, IaC Security, API Security, Secret Detection**, **Scorecard** or **AI Supply Chain Security**. - Confluence: **Secret Detection** only A key advantage of running scans via the API is the ability to apply configuration parameters to individual scans, overriding global tenant and project configurations. See [Explanation of Config](https://checkmarx.stoplight.io/docs/checkmarx-one-api-reference-guide/i20w1fceb1l15-run-a-scan#explanation-of-config) section below for tables detailing the various configuration options. ### Quick start **To run a scan:** 1. Identify a Project ID 2. Choose a scan source `type` (upload, git, or confluence). 3. Provide a `handler` object matching the source type 4. Select scanners in the `config` array 5. Submit the request to start the scan ### Minimum Request Structure Below is an example of the **minimum request structure** required to start a scan. - `type` and `handler` are explained [here](https://checkmarx.stoplight.io/docs/checkmarx-one-api-reference-guide/i20w1fceb1l15-run-a-scan#scan-source-types-and-handlers) - `project` is **required**. - `config` is explained [here](https://checkmarx.stoplight.io/docs/checkmarx-one-api-reference-guide/i20w1fceb1l15-run-a-scan#explanation-of-config) ```json { "type": "", "handler": {}, "project": { "id": "ee79f633-1ce1-4f0f-80e8-39cca31f8243" }, "config": [ { "type": "", "value": {} } ] } ``` ### Scan source types and handlers The `type` and `handler` fields in the request payload depend on the scan source type, such as a Zip archive, Git repository, or Confluence space. #### Examples: ```json "type": "upload", "handler": { "uploadurl": "https://master.cxast.com/storage/uploads.master.cxast.com-eu-west...", "uploadFormat": "" } ``` ```json "type": "git", "handler": { "repoUrl": "https://github.com/CheckmarxDev/ast-github-action", "branch": "master", "credentials": { "username": "your_user_name", "type": "apiKey", "value": "1234567890qwrtyuiopasdfghjkl;zxcvbnm,./" } } ``` ```json "type": "confluence", "handler": { "allSpaces": false, "spaceKeys": ["CNAS"], "url": "https://checkmarx.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/cnas", "credentials": { "username": "demo@example.com", "type": "apiToken", "value": "" } } ``` #### Notes on Confluence `handler` field - If `allSpaces` is set to `true`, the `spaceKeys` field is ignored.
- If `allSpaces` is `false`, at least one value must be provided in `spaceKeys`.
- To run a scan on only one page or set of pages in a Confluence space, replace `spaceKeys` with `pageIDs` and specify the IDs of the pages to scan. **For example:** `"pageIDs": ["7002554404"]` - Authentication is performed using a Confluence API token.
#### Notes on Upload `handler` field When running an SCA scan on an SBOM: submit the `uploadFormat` field with the value set to `single`. ### Explanation of `config`: The `config` field specifies which scanners to run and their configuration. (**sast, sca, kics** (i.e. IaC Security), **apisec, containers, microengines** (i.e., Secret Detection and Repo Health) and **aisc** (i.e.AI Supply Chain Security). > For Confluence scans, only `microengines` with `2ms` set as `true` is supported. Each scanner supports its own configuration parameters.

Expand the sections below to see the parameters supported by each scanner. Below the collapsible sections, we provide a complete configuration example containing every available parameter. You can copy the example as a starting point, then remove unused parameters and update the values to match your environment. > This information is intended to facilitate implementation. For additional context on the purpose of these configurations, follow the linked documentation for each scanner: [sast](https://docs.checkmarx.com/en/34965-338660-sast-configuration-options.html), [sca](https://docs.checkmarx.com/en/34965-349223-sca-configuration-options.html), [kics](https://docs.checkmarx.com/en/34965-349222-iac-security-configuration-options.html), [containers](https://docs.checkmarx.com/en/34965-357315-container-security-configuration-options.html), [apisec](), [secret detection](https://docs.checkmarx.com/en/34965-531300-secret-detection-configuration-options.html) and [aisc](https://docs.checkmarx.com/en/34965-695551-ai-supply-chain-security-configuration-options.html).
sast | Parameter | Description | Allowed Values | | --- | --- | --- | | `presetName` | Specifies the SAST preset containing the predefined security query set used for the scan (default: ASA Premium). | | `defaultConfigId` | | | `incremental` | Controls whether the scan analyzes only code changes since the last scan or performs a full scan of the entire codebase. | | `filter` | Includes or excludes specific files or folders from scanning using file patterns. | | `engineVerbose` | Controls scan engine logging level by enabling debug output or standard logging. | | `languageMode` | Defines whether scanning is optimized for a single primary language or multiple languages (default: multi). | | `fastScanMode` | Enables or disables Fast Scan mode to reduce scan time by optimizing analysis performance. |
sca | Parameter | Description | Allowed Values | | --- | --- | --- | | `filter` | Includes or excludes specific files or folders from SCA scanning using file pattern filters (wildcards supported, regex not supported). | | `exploitablePath` | Enables or disables analysis that determines whether vulnerable third-party dependencies are reachable from the source code. | | `lastSastScanTime` | Defines how many days a previous SAST scan can be reused for Exploitable Path analysis. | | `enableContainersScan` | Set to "false" when running the Containers scanner together with the SCA scanner | | `sbom` | Set as "true" to run a scan on an uploaded SBOM. See [here](https://checkmarx.stoplight.io/docs/checkmarx-one-api-reference-guide/59oydiz3mryzb-scans-service-rest-api#scanning-from-an-sbom-for-sca) for more info. |
kics (IaC Security) | Parameter | Description | Allowed Values | | --- | --- | --- | | `platforms` | Limits IaC scans to queries relevant only to the specified infrastructure platforms provided as a comma-separated list. | | `filter` | Includes or excludes specific files or folders from IaC security scanning using wildcard file patterns (regex not supported). | | `presetId` | Defines a specific preset of queries to be run in the scan. Must be a valid UUID. |
containers | Parameter | Description | Allowed Values | | --- | --- | --- | | `userCustomImages` | | | `filesFilter` | Includes or excludes specific files and folders from container scans using allow/block wildcard patterns. | | `imagesFilter` | Filters scanned container images by image name and/or tag using include or exclude wildcard patterns. | | `packagesFilter` | Excludes packages matching a regex pattern from cloud analysis while still listing them in scan results. | | `nonFinalStagesFilter` | Controls whether only final-stage Docker build images are scanned by excluding intermediate build stages. |

Generates a JWT access token used to authenticate all Checkmarx One API requests. ## Authentication Flows Select one of the following flows to obtain an access token:: - **API Key / Refresh Token**
Uses `grant_type`=`refresh_token` - **OAuth2 Client Credentials**
Uses `grant_type`=`client_credentials` ## Token Usage - Include the access token in all API requests using the Authorization header: `Authorization: Bearer ` - You can reuse the access token until it expires (**expires in 30 Minutes**) - When your access token expires, you can generate a new one using the **refresh_token** returned in the response (**valid for 8 hours**)
